bio_en:
Seong-Jin Cho is a pianist from Seoul, born in 1994.

In 2015 Cho became the first Korean to win the International Chopin Piano Competition (17th edition), which brought worldwide recognition. Cho studied with Professor Michel Béroff at the Conservatoire de Paris and, before that, with Professor Park Jin-young at the Korea National University of the Arts.

After placing third at the 2011 Tchaikovsky International Competition and third at the 2012 Rubinstein International Piano Competition, Cho reached a peak by winning the Chopin Competition in 2015. An exclusive contract with Deutsche Grammophon (DG) followed, and albums of music by Chopin, Debussy, Ravel, Rachmaninoff and others have been released.

Cho appears as a soloist with leading orchestras such as the Berlin Philharmonic, the London Symphony Orchestra and the Vienna Philharmonic, and gives recitals in major concert halls including Carnegie Hall, the Berlin Philharmonie and the Vienna Musikverein. Cho continues to perform energetically around the world.
style_en: Natural phrasing built on a delicate touch and poetic lyricism marks the playing. The approach is restrained, letting the music speak for itself without exaggeration.

bio_en:
Yunchan Lim is a pianist born in 2004 in Siheung, Gyeonggi Province.

In 2022 Lim won the 16th Van Cliburn International Piano Competition at the age of 18, the youngest winner in its history, and drew attention around the world. The win came while Lim was still a student at the Korea National University of the Arts, where Lim studied with Professor Minsoo Sohn.

After reaching the semifinals of the 2021 Ysaÿe International Piano Competition, Lim won over the jury and audience at the 2022 Van Cliburn Competition with Rachmaninoff's Piano Concerto No. 3 and Beethoven sonatas. Right after winning, Lim performed at Carnegie Hall, Lincoln Center, the Berlin Philharmonie and elsewhere.

In 2024 Lim signed an exclusive contract with Deutsche Grammophon (DG), and the first album for the label recorded works by Chopin and Liszt. Lim has appeared as a soloist with the Philadelphia Orchestra, the Los Angeles Philharmonic, the London Symphony Orchestra and others, and in the 2024-2025 season gave a recital tour of major cities in Europe and the United States. Lim is currently regarded as the young pianist attracting the most attention in the classical music world.
style_en: Overwhelming technique is combined with deep musical maturity, and the expressive power is grand yet delicate, especially in the Russian Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
Sunwook Kim is a pianist from Seoul, born in 1988.

Kim made an international debut in 2006 by winning the 14th Leeds International Piano Competition at the age of 18. Kim graduated from the Korea National University of the Arts and then studied at the Conservatoire de Paris with Michel Béroff and Pascal Devoyon.

After winning at Leeds, Kim established a position on the European scene by performing regularly with the London Symphony Orchestra, the Philharmonia Orchestra, the BBC Philharmonic and others. Kim completed a project cycle of the complete Beethoven piano sonatas, and is highly regarded in the German Romantic repertoire of Brahms, Schubert and Schumann.

Kim has released a number of albums on EMI Classics and Onyx Classics. Kim also performs actively with leading Korean orchestras such as the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra and the KBS Symphony Orchestra, and continues to perform mainly in Europe and Asia. Kim is currently also a professor at the Korea National University of the Arts, working to train the next generation.
style_en: An intellectual, structural approach is combined with a warm tone, and the playing shows excellent balance and depth, especially in the German Classical-Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
Yeol Eum Son is a pianist born in Gangneung in 1986.

Son won the silver medal at the 13th Van Cliburn International Piano Competition in 2011, and had previously won the Ettlingen International Competition in 2004. Son graduated from the Korea National University of the Arts and studied with Arie Vardi in Tel Aviv.

At the Van Cliburn Competition, Son was praised for performances of concertos by Beethoven and Prokofiev, and then signed an exclusive contract with EMI Classics (now Warner Classics). The repertoire is wide, from Beethoven, Liszt and Rachmaninoff to contemporary music, and Son gives distinctive interpretations especially of French Impressionist works and contemporary repertoire.

Son has performed with the New York Philharmonic, the Chicago Symphony Orchestra, the London Philharmonic Orchestra and others, and as a resident musician of the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra keeps close contact with Korean audiences. Son has released many recordings and is active in Korea and abroad.
style_en: The playing is well balanced: it rests on a clear touch and a logical sense of structure, yet never neglects emotional expression. Interpretive skill in contemporary repertoire is also excellent.

bio_en:
Bomsori Kim is a violinist from Seoul, born in 1989.

Kim won the violin category of the ARD International Music Competition in 2016, and had placed third at the Queen Elisabeth Competition in 2010. Kim studied with Professor Namyun Kim at the Korea National University of the Arts, and with Dorothy DeLay and Joseph Lin at the Juilliard School.

Kim plays a 1774 Guarneri del Gesù and has an exclusive contract with Warner Classics. Kim gives outstanding interpretations of major Romantic works such as the Tchaikovsky, Brahms and Sibelius violin concertos, and has appeared as a soloist with the London Philharmonic Orchestra, the Deutsches Symphonie-Orchester Berlin, the NHK Symphony Orchestra and others.

In 2017 Kim was a resident musician at Kumho Art Hall, and gives recitals in major concert halls in Korea and abroad. Kim is also an active chamber musician and collaborates with a variety of musicians. Kim currently performs actively, mainly in Europe and Asia.
style_en: A rich tone and lyrical expressiveness stand out. In Romantic works especially, the playing is both emotionally felt and technically perfect.

bio_en:
Clara-Jumi Kang is a Korean-German violinist, born in Mannheim in 1987.

In 2010 Kang won both the International Violin Competition of Indianapolis and the ARD International Music Competition in Munich, which brought worldwide attention. Kang studied with Valery Gradov at the Mannheim University of Music, and also studied at Juilliard.

Kang plays a 1710 Stradivarius and has an exclusive contract with Sony Classical. Kang has released albums of violin concertos by Brahms, Berg, Bruch, Sibelius and others, and gives deeply considered interpretations especially in the German repertoire.

Kang performs regularly as a soloist with leading orchestras such as the Berlin Philharmonic, the Vienna Philharmonic and the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, and is based in Europe. Kang is also an active chamber musician and takes part in a variety of music festivals.
style_en: Intense musical concentration and precise technique underlie modern yet profound interpretations, and the playing stays true to the German musical tradition.

bio_en:
Inmo Yang is a Korean violinist, born in 1986.

Yang graduated from the Korea National University of the Arts and studied with Professor Arie Vardi at the Hanover University of Music, Drama and Media in Germany. Yang has won prizes at major Korean competitions, and works mainly in the German Classical-Romantic repertoire of Beethoven, Schubert, Brahms and others.

Yang has given recitals at leading Korean concert halls such as the Seoul Arts Center and Lotte Concert Hall, and has been gaining experience performing with Korean orchestras. Yang is also active in chamber music and collaborates with a variety of performers. Yang is regarded as a performer who explores the essence of a work with a serious and sincere approach.
style_en: A serious and sincere approach explores the essence of each work, and the playing is reliable, especially in the German Classical repertoire.

bio_en:
Daejin Kim is a Korean pianist and educator, born in 1954.

A graduate of Seoul National University and the Juilliard School, Kim is a professor at the School of Music of the Korea National University of the Arts and plays a central role in classical music education in Korea. Kim is well known for having produced world-class pianists such as Yeol Eum Son, Seong-Jin Cho, Sunwook Kim and Ji-Young Moon.

Kim remains active as a performer too, appearing as a soloist with leading Korean orchestras and giving recitals. The repertoire is mainly the orthodox classical works of Beethoven, Schubert, Brahms and others, and Kim is especially active in chamber music.

Kim has contributed greatly to the development of classical music in Korea, and through teaching the next generation plays an important role in Korean pianists' advance onto the world stage. Kim continues to teach at the Korea National University of the Arts today.
style_en: Orthodox classical interpretation is valued, and the playing is clear and instructive, reflecting experience as an educator.

bio_en:
Hyungjun Kwon is a Korean pianist, born in 1989.

Kwon graduated from the Korea National University of the Arts and has won prizes at major Korean music competitions. Kwon plays repertoire from a range of periods and combines solo, concerto and chamber music activities.

Kwon gives recitals at leading Korean concert halls, gaining performing experience, and is gradually increasing appearances with Korean orchestras. As a pianist of the younger generation, Kwon continues to grow steadily, building a distinctive musical world through a variety of musical activities.
style_en: Works are approached with a serious attitude, and on the basis of reliable technique, musical depth is steadily added.

bio_en:
Danny Koo is a Korean-American violinist, born in 1997.

Koo graduated from the Juilliard School and performs in both the United States and Korea, moving between the two countries. Koo has placed in international competitions and plays a broad repertoire from classical to contemporary music.

Through playing with a youthful sensibility and active engagement on social media, Koo helps introduce classical music to younger audiences. Koo gives recitals at major concert halls in the United States and Korea and builds a career through a variety of opportunities to perform with orchestras.
style_en: A contemporary sensibility is combined with solid technique, and the repertoire is approached with the fresh outlook of a younger generation.

bio_en:
Dong-Hyek Lim is a pianist born in Seoul in 1984.

Lim made an international debut in 2001 by placing third at the 14th Leeds International Piano Competition at the age of 17. Lim graduated from the Korea National University of the Arts and studied with Professor Michel Béroff at the Conservatoire de Paris.

Lim is strong in the Romantic repertoire of Chopin, Liszt, Rachmaninoff and others, and is known for brilliant technique and passionate interpretations. Lim has performed with the London Philharmonic Orchestra, the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, the NHK Symphony Orchestra and others, and gives recitals at major concert halls in Korea and abroad.

Lim has released many recordings, and in Korea performs regularly with the KBS Symphony Orchestra, the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra and others. Lim is currently active mainly in Korea and Europe.
style_en: Dazzling technique is balanced with emotional expression, and the playing is passionate yet refined, especially in Romantic works.

bio_en:
Dong-Min Lim is a Korean pianist, born in 1980.

Lim studied piano in Germany, and besides a solo career is active as an accompanist and in chamber music. Lim performs at leading Korean concert halls and collaborates with a variety of musicians.

Lim has a reputation especially as an art-song accompanist and chamber musician, and appears on stage with leading Korean singers and instrumentalists. Lim also teaches, working to train younger musicians, and is regarded as a performer with outstanding skill in collaboration.
style_en: Delicate musicianship and outstanding collaborative skill mark the playing, which creates a harmonious ensemble, especially in chamber music.

bio_en:
Hyo-Sun Lim is a Korean soprano, born in 1980.

Lim studied voice in Italy and built a career on European opera stages. The repertoire is mainly Italian bel canto opera, with work in pieces by Rossini, Donizetti and Bellini.

Lim has gained performing experience at small and mid-sized opera houses in Europe, and in Korea appears in recitals and opera productions. With a clear, pure tone, Lim gives performances well suited to the bel canto repertoire, and continues to perform in Korea and abroad.
style_en: A clear, pure tone and accurate vocal technique make for performances well suited to Italian bel canto works.

bio_en:
Sumi Jo is a soprano born in Changwon in 1962.

Jo graduated from the Santa Cecilia Conservatory in Rome and made an international debut in 1986, chosen by Herbert von Karajan. On Karajan's recommendation, Jo appeared in Mozart operas at the Salzburg Festival and drew worldwide attention.

As a coloratura soprano, Jo showed outstanding ability in operas by Mozart, Rossini, Donizetti and others. Jo has performed on the stages of the world's leading opera houses, including the Metropolitan Opera, La Scala in Milan, the Vienna State Opera and Covent Garden.

Jo has released more than 50 albums and has helped introduce Korean art songs such as “Mongnyeonhwa” and “Gagopa” to the world. International recognition has included a Grammy nomination, and Jo was the first Korean singer to achieve worldwide fame. Jo remains active today in recitals and opera performances.
style_en: Dazzling coloratura technique and a pure, clear tone show the essence of bel canto opera, combining outstanding expressiveness with flawless technique.

bio_en:
Lang Lang is a pianist born in Shenyang, China, in 1982.

Lang began playing piano at the age of 5 and studied with Gary Graffman at the Curtis Institute of Music. In 1999 Lang became an overnight star by stepping in at short notice for André Watts at the Ravinia Festival in Chicago.

Lang has taken part in global events, performing at the opening ceremony of the 2008 Beijing Olympics and the closing ceremony of the 2018 Pyeongchang Olympics. An exclusive contract with Deutsche Grammophon followed, and albums of a wide range of repertoire, including Chopin, Tchaikovsky, Rachmaninoff and Beethoven, have been released.

Lang performs regularly as a soloist with leading orchestras such as the Berlin Philharmonic, the Vienna Philharmonic and the New York Philharmonic, and has given numerous concerts at Carnegie Hall, the Royal Albert Hall and elsewhere. In recognition of a contribution to making classical music popular, Lang also serves as a United Nations Messenger of Peace. Lang is currently one of the pianists who draw the largest audiences in the world.
style_en: Brilliant, dramatic playing captivates audiences, and the performances are marked by outstanding showmanship and an energetic stage presence.

bio_en:
Yuja Wang is a pianist born in Beijing in 1987.

After studying at the Central Conservatory of Music in Beijing, Wang went abroad at the age of 15 to the Mount Royal Conservatory in Canada. Wang then studied with Gary Graffman at the Curtis Institute of Music, where a career began in earnest.

Wang began to attract attention in 2007 with a concert with the Boston Symphony Orchestra, and captivated audiences around the world with overwhelming technique and a charismatic stage presence. An exclusive contract with Deutsche Grammophon followed, and albums of works by Rachmaninoff, Prokofiev, Ravel and others have been released.

Wang performs regularly with the Berlin Philharmonic, the Vienna Philharmonic, the New York Philharmonic and others, and shows outstanding interpretive skill especially in the Russian repertoire and contemporary music. Wang is also known for colorful outfits and a distinctive style, and has established a place as a new icon of classical music. Wang is currently one of the pianists with the busiest schedules in the world.
style_en: Lightning-fast technique, flawless playing, and intense energy and charisma stand out, with overwhelming force especially in Russian Romantic and contemporary works.

bio_en:
Daniil Trifonov is a pianist born in Nizhny Novgorod, Russia, in 1991.

In 2011 Trifonov won both the Rubinstein International Piano Competition and the Tchaikovsky International Competition, which brought worldwide attention. Trifonov studied with Sergei Babayan at the Cleveland Institute of Music and with Sergei Leschetizky in New York.

An exclusive contract with Deutsche Grammophon followed, and albums of works by Chopin, Liszt, Rachmaninoff, Tchaikovsky and others have been released, several of them nominated for Grammy Awards. Trifonov performs regularly as a soloist with leading orchestras such as the Berlin Philharmonic, the Vienna Philharmonic and the New York Philharmonic.

Besides being a pianist, Trifonov is also active as a composer and sometimes performs original works. Recitals are given at major concert halls around the world, including Carnegie Hall, the Vienna Musikverein and the Berlin Philharmonie. Trifonov is regarded as one of the leading pianists of this generation and is recognized as a performer who combines outstanding musicianship with technique.
style_en: Astonishing technique is joined by deep musical insight, and poetic yet intense expressiveness explores the essence of each work.

bio_en:
Yefim Bronfman is a pianist born in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, in 1958.

After emigrating to Israel, Bronfman studied at the Rubin Academy of Music, and later studied at the Juilliard School and the Curtis Institute of Music with Rudolf Firkušný, Leon Fleisher and Rudolf Serkin.

Bronfman won a Grammy Award in 1989 and has performed hundreds of times with the Berlin Philharmonic, the Vienna Philharmonic, the New York Philharmonic and others. Interpretations of piano concertos by Brahms, Prokofiev, Bartók and others are especially outstanding, and Bronfman is recognized as an authority on 20th-century music.

Bronfman has released many recordings on Sony Classical and has been active steadily on the world stage for more than 50 years. Valued for a powerful, clear touch and intellectual interpretations, Bronfman continues to perform actively today.
style_en: A powerful, clear touch and intellectual, structural interpretation characterize the playing, which carries authority especially in 20th-century repertoire.

bio_en:
Martha Argerich is a pianist born in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 1941.

After winning the Geneva International Competition and the Busoni Competition in 1957, Argerich won the International Chopin Piano Competition in 1965 and gained worldwide fame. Argerich studied with Friedrich Gulda in Vienna and with Nikita Magaloff in Switzerland.

Argerich gives outstanding interpretations of Romantic and 20th-century works by Ravel, Prokofiev, Chopin, Liszt and others, and is regarded as one of the world's finest chamber musicians as well. Numerous recordings have been released on Deutsche Grammophon, EMI and other labels, and several Grammy Awards have been won.

Argerich has performed countless times with the Berlin Philharmonic, the Vienna Philharmonic and others, and is famous for preferring chamber music and concerto work to solo playing. Argerich organizes the Lugano Festival, which bears the Argerich name, and supports young musicians. Now past eighty, Argerich remains very active and is regarded as a living legend.
style_en: Explosive energy and spontaneity, together with passionate yet poetic expression, mark the playing. Even amid improvisatory freedom, the technique is flawless.

bio_en:
Grigory Sokolov is a pianist born in Leningrad (now St. Petersburg), Russia, in 1950.

Sokolov made an international debut in 1966 by winning the Tchaikovsky International Competition at the age of 16. Sokolov studied with Moisei Khalfin at the Leningrad Conservatory and was regarded as the best pianist in the country from the Soviet era.

After the Soviet years, when contact with the Western world was limited, Sokolov began to perform in earnest on the European stage from the 1990s onward. The repertoire ranges widely from Bach to contemporary music, with profound interpretations especially of works by Bach, Beethoven, Schubert, Chopin and Brahms.

Sokolov is famous for making almost no studio recordings and concentrating on live performance, and the recitals sell out around the world. Known as a perfectionist, Sokolov overwhelms audiences with performances in which each piece is deeply absorbed. Regarded as one of the greatest living pianists, Sokolov has built a unique artistic world.
style_en: Perfect control of touch, deep concentration and meditative interpretations that seem to transcend time are the hallmarks, and the playing seems to breathe life into every note.

bio_en:
Evgeny Kissin is a pianist born in Moscow, Russia, in 1971.

Known as a prodigy, Kissin entered the special school of the Moscow Conservatory at the age of 6, and studied with Anna Pavlovna Kantor throughout life. A debut came at 12 with the Moscow Philharmonic, and in 1984 Kissin entered the Western stage by performing with the Berlin Philharmonic at Karajan's invitation.

After a 1990 debut at Carnegie Hall in New York, Kissin took a place among the world's finest pianists, and gives outstanding interpretations in the Romantic repertoire of Chopin, Liszt, Schumann, Brahms, Rachmaninoff and others. Many recordings have been released on Deutsche Grammophon, RCA, EMI and other labels, and several Grammy nominations have followed.

Kissin performs regularly with the Berlin Philharmonic, the Vienna Philharmonic, the New York Philharmonic and others, and gives recitals at major concert halls around the world. Valued for perfect technique and intense musical expressiveness, Kissin continues to perform as a top-ranking pianist.
style_en: Overwhelming technique, intense emotional expression and perfect control of tone color characterize the playing. In Romantic works especially, passion and lyricism are perfectly balanced.

bio_en:
Maurizio Pollini was a pianist born in Milan, Italy, in 1942. Pollini died in 2024.

In 1960, at the age of 18, Pollini won the International Chopin Piano Competition, and Artur Rubinstein, the chairman of the jury, praised the winner by saying, “Better than any of us.” Pollini studied with Carlo Lonati at the Milan Conservatory and later with Arturo Benedetti Michelangeli.

Pollini was recognized as a leading authority not only in the Classical-Romantic repertoire of Beethoven, Chopin, Schubert, Brahms and others but also in the interpretation of contemporary music by Schoenberg, Webern, Busoni, Nono, Stockhausen and others. An exclusive contract with Deutsche Grammophon lasted more than 60 years, and more than 100 albums were released.

Pollini performed countless times with the Berlin Philharmonic, the Vienna Philharmonic and others, and the collaboration with Claudio Abbado is especially famous. With a perfectionist approach and intellectual interpretations, Pollini was regarded as one of the leading pianists of the late 20th century.
style_en: Perfect technique, intellectual and structural interpretation, and a clear, transparent tone marked the playing, which showed outstanding insight in contemporary music as well.

bio_en:
András Schiff is a pianist and conductor born in Budapest, Hungary, in 1953.

Schiff studied with Pál Kadosa and Ferenc Rados at the Liszt Academy in Budapest and with George Malcolm in London. International attention began in 1974 with a prize at the Tchaikovsky International Competition.

Schiff is regarded as an authority on the Classical-Romantic repertoire of Bach, Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven, Schubert, Schumann and others, and is especially famous for performances of Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier and the complete Beethoven sonatas. More than 60 albums have been released on ECM, Decca, Teldec and other labels.

Besides a solo career, Schiff works as a conductor, sometimes leading the orchestra while playing concertos. Schiff is also an active chamber musician and works to train younger musicians through masterclasses. British citizenship has been acquired, and Schiff continues to be active on the world stage today.
style_en: A clear, transparent touch and a classical sense of balance and structure are central to the playing, which shows deep insight especially in interpretations of Bach and Beethoven.

bio_en:
Hilary Hahn is a violinist born in Lexington, Virginia, in 1979.

Hahn began the violin at the age of 3, entered the Curtis Institute of Music at 10 and studied with Jascha Brodsky. A debut came at 16 with the Baltimore Symphony, and since then Hahn has established a place as a top-ranking violinist.

Hahn gives outstanding interpretations of the orthodox repertoire, including Bach's solo sonatas and partitas and the violin concertos of Beethoven, Brahms and Sibelius, and actively premieres works commissioned from contemporary composers. Many recordings have been released on Deutsche Grammophon and Sony Classical, and three Grammy Awards have been won.

Hahn performs regularly with the Berlin Philharmonic, the Vienna Philharmonic, the New York Philharmonic and others, and gives recitals at major concert halls around the world. Hahn engages actively with audiences through social media and has also helped popularize classical music. Hahn is currently one of the most active violinists.
style_en: Perfect technique, accurate intonation, and clear, intellectual interpretations characterize the playing, which combines a modern sensibility with traditional interpretation in harmony.

bio_en:
Joshua Bell is a violinist born in Bloomington, Indiana, in 1967.

Bell began the violin at the age of 4 and studied with Josef Gingold at Indiana University, and later in Philadelphia with Joseph Fuchs, a pupil of Ivan Galamian. At 14, Bell made a debut with the Philadelphia Orchestra under Riccardo Muti.

Bell plays the 1989 Stradivarius “Gibson ex Huberman” and has released more than 40 albums on Sony Classical and Warner Classics. Bell gives outstanding interpretations of Romantic concertos by Bruch, Mendelssohn, Tchaikovsky, Brahms and others.

Bell became famous for a 2007 experiment in which a performance was given in disguise in a Washington, D.C. subway station, and is also known for playing the soundtrack of the film “The Red Violin.” Since 2011 Bell has been music director of the Academy of St Martin in the Fields, combining conducting with solo playing. Bell continues to perform actively on the world stage today.
style_en: A warm, rich tone and romantic, emotional interpretations characterize the playing, which has both popular appeal and artistry.

bio_en:
Anne-Sophie Mutter is a world-renowned violinist born in Rheinfelden, Germany, in 1963.

She began the violin at the age of 4 and is famous for being chosen by Herbert von Karajan at 13 and making her debut with the Berlin Philharmonic. She is highly regarded for exceptional technique and deep musicianship, and is also well known for her devotion to contemporary music, including premiering works by contemporary composers and having works dedicated to her.

She plays a broad spectrum of repertoire, from the classical to the contemporary, and has received numerous awards and decorations.
style_en: Her playing is based on refined technique and a wide range of bowing techniques, and combines emotional depth with intellectual interpretation.

bio_en:
Janine Jansen is a violinist born in Soest, the Netherlands, in 1978.

Jansen made a debut at the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam, and built an international reputation by performing with major orchestras in Europe and North America. Her playing is marked by intense emotional expression together with a refined, clear tone.

Jansen focuses mainly on chamber music and concertos, and plays a wide repertoire, from the classical works of Bach, Beethoven, Brahms and others to the 20th-century works of Britten, Shostakovich and others.
style_en: A clear, transparent tone and strong emotional contrasts stand out, with insightful interpretations of the repertoire.

bio_en:
Ray Chen is a violinist born in Taiwan in 1989 and raised in Australia.

Chen gained international fame by winning the Yehudi Menuhin International Violin Competition in 2008 and the Queen Elisabeth Competition in 2009 (as a joint winner). Besides outstanding technique, Chen is an artist who is also active in introducing classical music to the public through social media.
style_en: Dazzling technique is combined with a charismatic stage presence, and the playing is passionate and vivid.

bio_en:
Maxim Vengerov is a violinist and conductor born in Novosibirsk, Russia, in 1974.

Vengerov proved prodigious talent by taking first place at the Carl Flesch International Violin Competition in 1990. As a world-famous virtuoso, Vengerov has performed with all the major orchestras, and besides a solo career is very active as a teacher and conductor.
style_en: Explosive energy, the fiery emotion typical of the Russian school, and perfect technique come together in overwhelming playing.

bio_en:
Yo-Yo Ma is a world-renowned cellist born in Paris in 1955 to Chinese parents.

Ma has received numerous awards, including first prize at the Leventritt Competition in 1978, and is famous for innovative work that spans many genres, not only classical music but also tango, bluegrass and the Silk Road Ensemble.

Ma is devoted to cultural exchange through music and to contributing to society.
style_en: A deep, warm tone and great expressiveness go into a wide repertoire that crosses the musical boundaries between East and West.

bio_en:
Mischa Maisky is a cellist born in Riga, Latvia, in 1948.

Maisky is known as the only cellist to have studied with both Rostropovich and Piatigorsky, and won the Cassadó International Cello Competition in 1973. Famous for distinctive, strongly individual interpretations, Maisky showed deep insight especially in performances of Bach's unaccompanied cello suites.
style_en: Romantic, impassioned expression and a distinctive vibrato go with the pursuit of free, individual musical interpretation.

bio_en:
Steven Isserlis is a cellist born in London in 1958.

Isserlis is deeply versed in both the classical and contemporary repertoire, and has shown particular interest in period-instrument performance. His delicate, intellectual interpretations have been highly praised by critics.

Besides a solo career, Isserlis is also well known for active chamber music playing and for writing about music.
style_en: Intellectual, delicate interpretations and a clean, elegant tone characterize the playing, which values the structure and historical background of the work.

bio_en:
Gustavo Dudamel is a conductor born in Barquisimeto, Venezuela, in 1981.

A product of Venezuela's El Sistema education program, Dudamel drew worldwide attention by winning the Gustav Mahler Conducting Competition in 2004. Dudamel has held posts including music director of the Los Angeles Philharmonic and enjoys worldwide fame.

Intense energy and lively interpretations captivate audiences.
style_en: A vigorous, passionate conducting style shows excellent expressiveness, especially in the Romantic and 20th-century repertoire.

bio_en:
Yannick Nézet-Séguin is a conductor born in Montreal, Canada, in 1975.

Nézet-Séguin is active worldwide, having served as music director of the Philadelphia Orchestra and of the Metropolitan Opera, among other posts. Nézet-Séguin is a maestro highly regarded for a broad repertoire and strong leadership.
style_en: A flexible, dynamic conducting style draws deep musicality and emotional playing from the orchestra in both opera and symphonic works.

bio_en:
Sir Simon Rattle is a world-renowned conductor born in Liverpool, England, in 1955.

Rattle established a place as a master of the world classical scene as chief conductor of the Berlin Philharmonic from 2002 to 2018. Rattle is currently chief conductor of the Bavarian Radio Symphony Orchestra.

Rattle is particularly well versed in 20th-century and contemporary music.
style_en: Sharp analytical ability and delicate detail are valued, and complex contemporary music is realized with clarity.

bio_en:
Ilya Rashkovskiy is a pianist born in Russia in 1985.

Rashkovskiy has won prizes at numerous international competitions, including first prize at the Hamamatsu International Piano Competition and a prize at the Queen Elisabeth Competition. Rashkovskiy is noted for delicate and deep musicianship.
style_en: Resting on a warm, lyrical tone, delicate and poetic playing conveys deep feeling.

bio_en:
Boris Giltburg is a pianist born in Moscow, Russia, in 1984 and raised in Israel.

Giltburg won the Queen Elisabeth Competition in 2013 and gained worldwide fame. Known for outstanding technique and intense expressiveness, Giltburg is especially strong in the playing of Rachmaninoff and Prokofiev.
style_en: Resting on a firm touch and overwhelming technique, the playing expresses explosive energy and deep lyricism at the same time.

bio_en:
Pavel Kolesnikov is a pianist born in Novosibirsk, Russia, in 1989.

Kolesnikov has won prizes at many competitions, including first prize at the 2012 Jorge Bolet International Piano Competition, and has drawn the attention of critics with delicate and original interpretations. Kolesnikov is active on major stages such as Carnegie Hall.
style_en: A delicate style of playing, marked by colorful tone and fluent phrasing, with works interpreted from an original perspective.

bio_en:
Alexandra Dovgan is an up-and-coming pianist born in Russia in 2007.

Dovgan won the Moscow International Grand Piano Competition in 2018 and drew international attention. Despite a young age, Dovgan is regarded as having deep musicality and astonishing technique.
style_en: Interpretations mature beyond the performer's years, solid technique and a clean, deep tone are the hallmarks.

bio_en:
Lucas Debargue is a pianist born in Paris in 1990.

Although Debargue took fourth place at the 2015 Tchaikovsky International Competition, great attention came from the public and critics, along with the Moscow Music Critics' Prize for original musicality and interpretations. A broad repertoire, from the classical to the modern, is interpreted from a distinctive perspective.
style_en: A strongly individual artist, known for free, spontaneous playing, deep insight and a sensitive, distinctive tone.

bio_en:
Nobuyuki Tsujii is a visually impaired pianist born in Tokyo, Japan, in 1988.

Tsujii gained worldwide fame by sharing first prize at the Van Cliburn International Piano Competition in 2009. His playing captivates audiences with outstanding technique together with deep lyricism and moving expressiveness.
style_en: A delicate touch and rich emotional expression give the playing a deep resonance, and it is especially strong in the Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
Bruce Liu is a pianist born in Paris in 1997 and raised in Canada.

Liu won the 18th International Chopin Piano Competition in 2021 and gained international fame. Combining outstanding technique with refined musicianship, Liu has been active around the world since the win.
style_en: A refined style in which dazzling technique, sharp intellect and a free, flowing line are in harmony.

bio_en:
Kyohei Sorita is a pianist born in Japan in 1990.

Sorita drew worldwide attention by taking second place at the 18th International Chopin Piano Competition in 2021. Active on the international stage beyond Japan, Sorita also works as a conductor, leading the Japan National Orchestra, which Sorita founded.
style_en: Strong, dynamic attack and playing on a grand scale, with an emphasis on dramatic expressiveness.

bio_en:
Martin García García is a pianist born in Spain in 1996.

García García drew attention by taking third place at the 18th International Chopin Piano Competition in 2021. Well received for delicate sensibility and deep musicianship, García García continues an international career mainly in Europe and Asia.
style_en: A warm, lyrical tone and elegant, delicate phrasing, with an emphasis on natural flow.

bio_en:
Hao Rao is a pianist born in China in 2001.

Rao drew attention as the youngest participant at the 2021 Van Cliburn International Piano Competition and was well received for deep musicianship. Rao is currently active on the international stage and continues to prove that ability.
style_en: Accurate technique goes together with delicate emotional expression, and the playing is especially at home in the Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
Leonora Armellini is a pianist born in Padua, Italy, in 1992.

Armellini gained international fame by placing fifth at the 18th International Chopin Piano Competition in 2021. One of Italy's leading young pianists, Armellini is strong in the Classical-Romantic repertoire.
style_en: The playing inherits the Italian pianistic tradition and interprets works with a bright, clear tone and fluent technique.

bio_en:
J J Jun Li Bui is a pianist born in Toronto, Canada, in 2004.

Bui drew attention at the 18th International Chopin Piano Competition in 2021 as the youngest prizewinner (sixth place). A rising young artist, Bui shows a delicate touch and musical depth.
style_en: A delicate, thoughtful touch and steady playing join musical structure with lyricism.

bio_en:
Kyung Wha Chung is a world-renowned violinist born in South Korea in 1948.

Chung made an international debut by winning the Edgar Leventritt Competition in 1967. Charismatic playing and deep expressiveness have made Chung one of the finest violinists of the late 20th century, and a worldwide reputation was built both as a soloist and as a member of the Chung Trio.
style_en: A leading Korean master violinist whose playing carries intense absorption, explosive energy and deep, passionate feeling.

bio_en:
Myung-Whun Chung is a world-renowned conductor and pianist born in South Korea in 1953.

Chung drew attention by taking second place in the piano category of the Tchaikovsky International Competition in 1974, then turned to conducting and became the first Asian to gain worldwide fame as a conductor. Chung has served as principal conductor of major institutions, including the Opéra Bastille in Paris, the Santa Cecilia Orchestra in Rome and the Tokyo Philharmonic Orchestra.
style_en: The orchestra is led with a soft, fluent conducting style and deep insight, and the results are outstanding especially in the Romantic repertoire and operatic interpretation.

bio_en:
Haydn Kwon is an up-and-coming pianist born in South Korea in 2001.

Standing out at competitions in Korea and abroad, Kwon is growing into a next-generation pianist, combining delicate sensibility with outstanding technique.
style_en: Built on a delicate, lyrical touch and clean interpretation, the playing centers on the Classical and Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
Minkyung Baek is a violinist born in South Korea in 1998.

Baek is building a career as a performer, having won prizes at many competitions in Korea and abroad, and is drawing attention for reliable ability and rich expressiveness.
style_en: Balanced technique and a warm tone convey music that is comfortable for a general audience yet still deep.

bio_en:
Doori Na is a violinist born in South Korea in 1995.

Na is a young performer active in many fields, including solo work, orchestral concertmaster duties and chamber music, and handles a broad musical spectrum.
style_en: A precise, clear style of playing, with depth added to interpretation through a scholarly approach to each work.

bio_en:
Junchan Kim is an up-and-coming pianist born in South Korea in 2003.

Standing out at competitions in Korea and abroad from a young age, Kim is the subject of high expectations and is growing into a young master with great potential.
style_en: Dynamic energy and delicate sensitivity coexist in the playing, which conveys a deep resonance.

bio_en:
David Hwang is a pianist born in South Korea in 1980.

Hwang is active in performance and teaching in Korea and abroad, and is a capable artist with a wide-ranging repertoire. Hwang is particularly active in chamber music as well.
style_en: Built on solid fundamentals and reliable playing, this is a style that pursues the orthodoxy of classical music.

bio_en:
Hyun-Ah Song is a soprano born in South Korea in 1985.

Song is active on opera stages and in concerts in Korea and abroad, and is well received for a clear, rich tone and excellent acting.
style_en: Delicate emotional lines and clean high notes underlie the singing, which is particularly strong in the Italian opera repertoire.

bio_en:
Taehyun Kim is a violinist born in South Korea in 2000.

Standing out at competitions in Korea and abroad at a young age, Kim is drawing attention, combining solid fundamentals with individual musical interpretation.
style_en: Excellent technique and depth of musical interpretation allow Classical and Romantic works to be played with refinement.

bio_en:
Ji-Yoon Lee is a violinist born in South Korea in 1997.

Lee is building a career as a soloist and chamber musician on the international stage, including in Europe, and shows delicate, insightful musicianship.
style_en: Clear articulation and intellectual interpretation stand out, and the playing expresses the form and structure of a work clearly.

bio_en:
Hee-Chul Bae is a pianist born in South Korea in 1970.

Bae trains the next generation at a Korean university while pursuing research and performance alongside, and plays a broad repertoire.
style_en: A traditional, reliable style of playing, focused on conveying the deep emotion of each work.

bio_en:
Jinhee Kim is a pianist born in South Korea in 1978.

Kim is active in solo and chamber music in Korea and abroad and is regarded as a performer with outstanding technique and delicate expressiveness.
style_en: Fluent technique and a rich, varied palette of tone color bring out the Romantic feeling of a work to the fullest.

bio_en:
Taek Gi Lee is a cellist born in South Korea in 1985.

After studying in Europe and elsewhere, Lee has been active on stages in Korea and abroad, a player who brings out the deep, rich tone of the cello well.
style_en: A warm, lyrical tone and reliable playing underlie performances of the Classical and Romantic cello repertoire.

bio_en:
Mun-Sung Kim is a violinist born in South Korea in 1973.

Kim connects with audiences through solo work and appearances as a soloist with leading Korean orchestras, and is a seasoned performer with a wide repertoire.
style_en: Orthodox interpretation and seasoned technique underlie playing that values the completeness of the work and musical balance.

bio_en:
Igor Levit is a pianist born in Nizhny Novgorod, Russia, in 1987.

In 2005 Levit won second prize and a special prize at the Arthur Rubinstein International Piano Master Competition. Levit has won critical acclaim for outstanding ability in performing the complete Beethoven sonatas and in interpreting difficult contemporary repertoire.

Levit also has great influence through live performances that carry social messages and through online activity.
style_en: Intellectual, innovative interpretation and perfect technique underlie playing that explores the structure and philosophical depth of a work.

bio_en:
Murray Perahia is a pianist born in New York in 1947.

Perahia won the Leeds International Piano Competition in 1972 and gained worldwide fame, and is counted an authority in the Classical and Romantic repertoire of Mozart, Beethoven, Chopin, Schumann and others.

With an intellectual, elegant style of playing, Perahia has left many outstanding recordings and has won several Grammy Awards.
style_en: Elegant, classical playing that combines a clear, delicate touch, fluent phrasing and deep lyricism.

bio_en:
Piotr Anderszewski is a pianist born in Warsaw, Poland, in 1969.

Anderszewski became famous for an incident at the 1990 Leeds International Piano Competition in which Anderszewski stopped playing during the final and withdrew, and afterwards drew critical attention for original interpretations and strong individuality. Anderszewski has built a distinctive domain especially in Bach, Beethoven, Schumann, Chopin and others.
style_en: Strong individuality and intellectual insight underlie original performances that are unpredictable yet logically structured.

bio_en:
Radu Lupu is a pianist born in Galați, Romania, in 1945.

Lupu won the Van Cliburn International Piano Competition in 1966, the George Enescu International Competition in 1967 and the Leeds International Piano Competition in 1969, sweeping the top competitions. In contrast to a reclusive private life, Lupu was revered for deep, lyrical playing.

The interpretations of Schubert, Mozart and Brahms in particular were unrivaled.
style_en: A deep, warm tone and quiet yet intense lyricism underlie philosophical playing that probes the essence of a work.

bio_en:
Marc-André Hamelin is a pianist born in Montreal, Canada, in 1961.

Hamelin is famous for astonishing technique and a wide repertoire, in particular for unearthing and performing technically difficult or little-known works. Many recordings have been released on the Hyperion label.
style_en: Phenomenal technique and intellectual precision allow everything from the standard repertoire to works of transcendental virtuosity to be played flawlessly.

bio_en:
Benjamin Grosvenor is a pianist born in England in 1992.

Grosvenor drew attention by winning BBC Young Musician of the Year in 2004 as the youngest winner. Active on the world stage, Grosvenor is noted for playing marked by a delicate touch and lyrical expressiveness.
style_en: A clear, transparent tone and elegant phrasing underlie a sensitivity that is particularly outstanding in the Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
Alexander Melnikov is a pianist born in Moscow, Russia, in 1973.

Melnikov made a debut at the Lucerne Festival at the invitation of Claudio Abbado, and is famous for playing a vast repertoire from the classical to the contemporary, moving between period and modern instruments.
style_en: A sharp intellect and scholarly interpretation underlie vivid playing that also values historical research.

bio_en:
Víkingur Ólafsson is a pianist born in Iceland in 1984.

Ólafsson achieved great success with original reinterpretations of the Classical-era repertoire of Bach, Mozart and others, and gained worldwide fame through albums released on Deutsche Grammophon.
style_en: A clear touch, delicate pedaling, and original programming and interpretation present classical music with a modern sensibility.

bio_en:
Jan Lisiecki is a pianist of Polish descent, born in Alberta, Canada, in 1995.

Lisiecki drew attention by performing with leading orchestras from a young age. Lisiecki shows deep insight especially in Chopin and Mozart, and is an exclusive artist of Deutsche Grammophon.
style_en: A clear, clean tone and natural breathing underlie playing that emphasizes musical lyricism over virtuosity.

bio_en:
Kit Armstrong is a pianist and composer born in Los Angeles in 1992.

Armstrong showed genius in many fields, including mathematics, science and music, and received instruction from Alfred Brendel. Armstrong is particularly renowned for interpretations of Bach and Mozart and is known for intellectual, thoughtful playing.
style_en: Extremely precise and analytical interpretation underlies scholarly playing that clearly reveals the structure and logic of a work.

bio_en:
Francesco Piemontesi is a pianist born in Switzerland in 1983.

Piemontesi began an international career after winning a prize at the Queen Elisabeth Competition, and shows outstanding talent especially in the interpretation of Mozart and Schumann. A delicate touch and deep lyricism go together.
style_en: A delicate, transparent tone underlies playing that harmonizes structural clarity with Romantic sensibility.

bio_en:
Paul Lewis is a pianist born in Liverpool, England, in 1972.

A pupil of Alfred Brendel, Lewis gained worldwide fame especially for performances of the complete Beethoven sonatas. The playing is characterized by intellectual and deep interpretation together with outstanding lyricism.
style_en: Thoughtful, intellectual interpretation and a clean, clear touch express the structural beauty and depth of the Classical repertoire.

bio_en:
Stephen Hough is a pianist, composer and writer born in England in 1961.

Hough gained international fame by winning the Naumburg International Piano Competition in 1983. Known for enormous technique together with intellectual, deep interpretations, Hough works especially to unearth little-known repertoire from the Romantic era.

Hough is a MacArthur Fellow and is a professor at several universities.
style_en: Perfect technique and a wide repertoire underlie unique, intellectual interpretations that seem timeless.

bio_en:
Jean-Efflam Bavouzet is a pianist born in France in 1962.

Bavouzet began to attract attention by winning the Cologne International Piano Competition in 1986. Bavouzet is well established as an interpreter of French repertoire such as Debussy and Ravel and of Classical repertoire such as Beethoven and Haydn.

Besides solo work, Bavouzet is also active as a conductor and educator.
style_en: A clear, clean touch and a distinctly French style of playing that delicately reveals the structure and color of a work.

bio_en:
Bertrand Chamayou is a pianist born in Toulouse, France, in 1981.

Considered one of France's leading young pianists for outstanding technique and sensibility, Chamayou has shown deep interpretations across a varied repertoire that includes Chopin, Liszt and Ravel.

Chamayou has won the French Victoires de la Musique Classique award several times.
style_en: Intense expressiveness and brilliant technique, with a colorful palette of tone especially in the Romantic and French repertoire.

bio_en:
Leonidas Kavakos is a violinist born in Athens, Greece, in 1967.

By winning the Sibelius International Violin Competition in 1985 and the Paganini International Violin Competition in 1988, Kavakos was recognized as a master of worldwide stature, combining a sharp intellect with perfect technique.

Kavakos is also active as a conductor and performs with major orchestras.
style_en: Precise, intellectual interpretation and a clean, dense tone, with a modern insight that is particularly striking.

bio_en:
Midori Goto is a violinist born in Osaka, Japan, in 1971.

Midori drew attention for prodigious talent by making a debut with the New York Philharmonic at the age of 11. Since then, deep musicianship combined with social contribution has maintained a worldwide reputation.

Midori is particularly well known for dedication to education and community activities.
style_en: Outstanding technique and concentration underlie an intellectual, delicate style of playing that conveys a deep resonance through emotional restraint.

bio_en:
Itzhak Perlman is a violinist and conductor born in Tel Aviv, Israel, in 1945.

Perlman established a worldwide reputation by winning the Leventritt Competition in 1964. One of the great violin masters of the late 20th century, Perlman combines a warm, rich tone, perfect technique and popular appeal.

Perlman is also devoted to music education and to advancing the rights of people with disabilities.
style_en: A warm, human tone, perfect technique and deep lyricism underlie a romantic style of playing.

bio_en:
James Ehnes is a violinist born in Canada in 1976.

Ehnes drew attention by winning the Schiff Foundation Young Artists Award in 1994. Skilled in both classical and contemporary repertoire, Ehnes was praised especially for performances of Bach's solo sonatas and partitas.

Ehnes has won many Grammy and Juno Awards.
style_en: Accurate, clean technique and a transparent tone are combined with a scholarly approach to the work and delicate expression.

bio_en:
Jennifer Koh is a violinist born in the United States in 1976.

Koh drew attention by winning the silver medal at the Tchaikovsky International Competition in 1994. Known especially for deep devotion to contemporary music, Koh has premiered and commissioned works by numerous contemporary composers.

Koh broadens the boundaries of classical music through self-organized projects.
style_en: Intellectual, passionate interpretation and outstanding technique clearly reveal the complex structures of contemporary music in particular.

bio_en:
Daniel Hope is a violinist born in Durban, South Africa, in 1974.

A student of Menuhin, Hope actively unearths and performs little-known works and works by contemporary composers, in addition to major repertoire such as Beethoven and Brahms.

Hope has also been a member of the Kronos Quartet, and since 2020 has served as music director of the Zurich Opera.
style_en: A warm tone and fluent phrasing show deep lyricism, and the storytelling ability to combine music and narrative is outstanding.

bio_en:
Ning Feng is a violinist born in China in 1981.

Feng won the Paganini International Violin Competition in 2006 and gained international fame. The playing is characterized by a fusion of precise technique and Eastern lyricism.

Feng currently lives in Berlin and is active mainly in Europe and Asia.
style_en: Clear technique and delicate sensibility, with insight shown particularly in Romantic concertos.

bio_en:
Baiba Skride is a violinist born in Latvia in 1981.

Skride began an international career through second place at the Queen Elisabeth Competition in 2001, and plays a wide musical spectrum from the classical repertoire to 20th-century repertoire.

Her two younger sisters, Lauma and Linda, are also well-known performers.
style_en: Accurate, powerful playing and deep musical maturity, well known for balanced interpretation.

bio_en:
Augustin Hadelich is a violinist born in Germany in 1984.

Hadelich drew attention by winning the International Violin Competition of Indianapolis in 2006. With lyrical yet intellectual interpretations and outstanding technique, Hadelich performs with leading orchestras around the world.

Hadelich won a Grammy Award in 2016.
style_en: A clean, transparent tone, excellent technique, and delicate, thoughtful musicianship.

bio_en:
Alina Ibragimova is a violinist born in Russia in 1985.

Skilled in both period-instrument performance and contemporary repertoire, Ibragimova is especially well established for interpretations of Bach's unaccompanied works, and is famous for an intellectual, ascetic style of playing.

Besides solo work, Ibragimova is also active in chamber music.
style_en: Refined, intellectual interpretation and a pure tone underlie playing that emphasizes the structural beauty of a work.

bio_en:
Vilde Frang is a violinist born in Norway in 1986.

Frang drew attention by winning the Credit Suisse Young Artist Award in 2012, and combines the lyricism of the Scandinavian school with cool analytical ability.

Many recordings have been released on the EMI Classics label.
style_en: Intense absorption, refined technique and deeply lyrical playing that carries Scandinavian feeling.

bio_en:
Sol Gabetta is a cellist born in Argentina in 1981.

Gabetta drew international attention by winning the Credit Suisse Young Artist Award in 2004, and performs with leading orchestras around the world with passionate playing and a beautiful tone.

Gabetta plays a wide repertoire, from the Baroque era to contemporary music.
style_en: Vigorous, passionate expressiveness and romantic playing that brings out the warm, rich sound of the cello to the fullest.

bio_en:
Gautier Capuçon is a cellist born in France in 1981.

One of France's leading cellists, Capuçon has been active in chamber music with his older brother Renaud Capuçon (a violinist), and is famous for an elegant, refined style of playing.
style_en: Elegant, refined phrasing and a deep, rich tone, with playing that carries French-style lyricism.

bio_en:
Alban Gerhardt is a cellist born in Germany in 1969.

Gerhardt drew attention by winning the Leventhal Competition (Lievenskonskors) in 1993. On the basis of a deep understanding of contemporary music, Gerhardt plays a wide variety of works and is also active in socially engaged activities.
style_en: Intense absorption and delicate expressiveness, handling complex repertoire from the classical to the contemporary with ease.

bio_en:
Sheku Kanneh-Mason is a cellist born in England in 1999.

Kanneh-Mason drew attention by winning BBC Young Musician of the Year in 2016, and gained worldwide popularity by performing at the wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle.
style_en: A warm, appealing tone and deep lyricism, playing that shows the popular appeal of classical music well.

bio_en:
Jean-Guihen Queyras is a cellist born in France in 1967.

Queyras is active over a wide range, from the classical repertoire to contemporary music and period-instrument performance. Famous for intellectual, reflective playing, Queyras combines chamber music with solo work.
style_en: Precise, intellectual interpretation and flexible changes of tone color express the subtle nuances of a work superbly.

bio_en:
Johannes Moser is a cellist born in Germany in 1979.

Moser drew international attention by taking second place at the Tchaikovsky International Competition in 2002, and is famous for an intense, charismatic style of playing.

Besides the Classical and Romantic repertoire, Moser actively plays 20th-century and contemporary works.
style_en: Brilliant, dynamic technique and intense expressiveness show deep absorption in the work and individual interpretation.

bio_en:
Truls Mørk is a cellist born in Norway in 1961.

Mørk has won prizes at many international competitions, including sixth place at the Tchaikovsky International Competition in 1982, and is famous for playing that combines Nordic lyricism with deep musicianship.
style_en: A deep, rich cello tone and lyrical sensitivity, strong particularly in Romantic and contemporary repertoire such as Dvořák and Shostakovich.

bio_en:
Kian Soltani is a cellist of Iranian descent, born in Austria in 1992.

Soltani drew attention by winning the Credit Suisse Young Artist Award in 2017. Active as a soloist, chamber musician and conductor, Soltani is growing into a young master.
style_en: Outstanding technique and Eastern lyricism, leaving a strong impression through a wide range of pitch and emotional expression.

bio_en:
Camille Thomas is a cellist born in France in 1988.

Thomas built a career studying in Germany and is drawing attention for an elegant, delicate style of playing, with strengths particularly in French repertoire and Romantic works.
style_en: Soft, fluent phrasing and a clear tone, expressing a delicate sensibility peculiar to a female cellist.

bio_en:
Christian Thielemann is a conductor born in Berlin, Germany, in 1959.

Considered the foremost living authority on German Romantic repertoire and on the music of Wagner and Richard Strauss, Thielemann has worked on world-class stages including the Bayreuth Festival and the Vienna Philharmonic.

From 2025 Thielemann is due to become general music director of the Berlin State Opera.
style_en: Pursuing the interpretation of the orthodox German school, this conducting realizes works through grand, deep sound and philosophical insight.

bio_en:
Sir Antonio Pappano is a conductor born in England in 1959.

Pappano is a master of opera and orchestral conducting who has served as music director of the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden, and music director of the Santa Cecilia Orchestra in Rome, among other posts. Pappano is especially well established in Italian opera and in the interpretation of Verdi and Puccini.
style_en: Drawing on opera conducting experience, the conducting is rich in dramatic and emotional expression and draws fiery energy from the orchestra.

bio_en:
Iván Fischer is a conductor and composer born in Budapest, Hungary, in 1951.

Fischer gained worldwide fame by co-founding and leading the Budapest Festival Orchestra in 1983. His conducting is famous for original interpretation and delicate coordination of the ensemble.
style_en: Original interpretation that combines delicate detail with humor, showing depth especially in the Classical and Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
Mariss Jansons is a conductor born in Riga, Latvia, in 1943.

Jansons built a reputation as chief conductor of the world's finest orchestras, including the Oslo Philharmonic, the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra and the Bavarian Radio Symphony Orchestra. Jansons is especially strong in Russian and Romantic repertoire.
style_en: A maestro who draws out the dynamic sound of the orchestra through precise, balanced interpretation and intense drive.

bio_en:
Valery Gergiev is a conductor born in Moscow, Russia, in 1953.

Gergiev led Russian musical life as artistic and general director of the Mariinsky Theatre. Famous for explosive energy and a charismatic conducting style, Gergiev is especially well versed in the interpretation of Russian opera and symphonies.
style_en: Intense, spontaneous energy and charismatic conducting that maximizes the fiery emotion typical of Russian music.

bio_en:
Riccardo Chailly is a conductor born in Milan, Italy, in 1953.

Chailly has served as chief conductor of major orchestras, including the Berlin Radio Symphony Orchestra, the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra and the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra. Skilled in both opera and symphonic works, Chailly shows deep insight especially in the interpretation of Mahler and Bruckner.
style_en: Precise, clear conducting combined with Italian sensibility, expressing the structure and dynamism of a work delicately.

bio_en:
Kirill Petrenko is a conductor born in Omsk, Russia, in 1972.

Petrenko is currently chief conductor of the Berlin Philharmonic and is regarded as one of the finest conductors alive today for outstanding musical maturity and deep interpretation. Petrenko is also known for being extremely averse to media exposure.
style_en: Thorough score analysis and detailed expression give complete control of the orchestra, delivering intense absorption and depth.

bio_en:
François-Xavier Roth is a conductor born in Paris in 1971.

Roth founded Les Siècles, an ensemble specializing in contemporary music, and takes an innovative approach, moving between period and modern instruments. Roth is especially well established for interpretations of French repertoire.
style_en: Dynamic, innovative conducting, with experimental interpretation that brings out both the historical context of a work and a modern sensibility.

bio_en:
Andris Nelsons is a conductor born in Riga, Latvia, in 1978.

Nelsons concurrently serves as music director of the Boston Symphony Orchestra and the Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra, and shows outstanding ability especially in the late Romantic repertoire of Bruckner, Mahler, Shostakovich and others.
style_en: A passionate, energetic conducting style with fluent arm movements, drawing grand, deep sound from the orchestra.

bio_en:
Diana Damrau is a soprano born in Germany in 1971.

One of the finest lyric coloratura sopranos alive today, Damrau shows flawless technique and delicate acting in operatic repertoire by Mozart, Donizetti, Verdi and others. Damrau is especially famous for the role of the Queen of the Night.
style_en: A queen of opera who combines perfect technique, a clear, rich tone and outstanding acting that commands the stage.

bio_en:
Renée Fleming is a soprano born in the United States in 1959.

Called the queen of living lyric sopranos, Fleming sings a wide repertoire that includes Mozart, Richard Strauss and Italian opera. Her warm, rich voice has been loved around the world.
style_en: A warm, velvety tone and elegant, delicate phrasing, showing deep lyricism and musical maturity.

bio_en:
Pretty Yende is a soprano born in South Africa in 1985.

Yende drew attention by winning prizes at many international competitions, including the Viotti International Competition. Performing at leading opera houses such as the Metropolitan Opera and La Scala, Yende is strong in coloratura repertoire.
style_en: Dazzling technique, a clear, pure tone and explosive energy leave a strong impression on the opera stage.

bio_en:
Sabine Devieilhe is a soprano born in France in 1985.

Devieilhe is a coloratura soprano who shows outstanding ability in French repertoire and Mozart operas. Her delicate, light tone suits Baroque and early Romantic works.
style_en: A clear, light tone and excellent coloratura technique, with a unique domain especially in French Baroque and Mozart.

bio_en:
Aleksandra Kurzak is a soprano born in Poland in 1977.

Kurzak sings leading roles at the world's major opera houses, including the Metropolitan Opera and the Royal Opera House. Kurzak is strong in bel canto and Italian opera repertoire.
style_en: Brilliant, flexible coloratura technique combined with a warm lyric tone, particularly excellent in Donizetti and Puccini.

bio_en:
Maria Agresta is a soprano born in Italy in 1975.

One of Italy's leading lyric sopranos, Agresta sings leading roles in Italian opera by Verdi, Puccini and others on major stages such as La Scala and the Metropolitan Opera.
style_en: A rich, dramatic lyric tone and ardent emotional expression give an overwhelming presence especially in the operas of Verdi and Puccini.

bio_en:
Jonas Kaufmann is a tenor born in Munich, Germany, in 1969.

Considered one of the finest tenors alive today, Kaufmann handles a broad spectrum covering Italian, French and German repertoire. His dark, rich tone and excellent acting are unrivaled.
style_en: A dark, rich tone, dramatic expressiveness, and perfect diction and acting combine in an exemplar of the dramatic tenor.

bio_en:
Juan Diego Flórez is a tenor born in Lima, Peru, in 1973.

An authority on the bel canto repertoire of Rossini, Donizetti, Bellini and others, Flórez is famous for coloratura technique that handles the high C flawlessly, and is counted the finest leggero tenor alive today.
style_en: A clear, light tone and astonishing coloratura technique have built a unique domain in bel canto opera.

bio_en:
Piotr Beczała is a tenor born in Poland in 1969.

Beczała sings leading roles in Italian and French opera at the world's major opera houses. The warm, lyrical lyric-tenor voice is loved around the world.
style_en: A warm, lyrical lyric-tenor sound and elegant, accurate vocal production, with strengths in bel canto and Romantic opera.

bio_en:
Michael Fabiano is a tenor born in the United States in 1984.

Fabiano drew attention by winning prizes at major competitions, including the Domingo International Vocal Competition. With intense energy and outstanding vocal ability, Fabiano sings leading roles in Italian opera.
style_en: A dynamic, powerful voice and dramatic expressiveness leave a deep impression in Italian Romantic opera.

bio_en:
Javier Camarena is a tenor born in Mexico in 1976.

A coloratura tenor, Camarena is regarded as a bel canto specialist, the successor to Juan Diego Flórez. Camarena has outstanding technique, handling the high C and other high notes with ease.
style_en: A clear, penetrating tone and astonishing handling of high notes make for the pinnacle of the bel canto repertoire, such as Rossini and Donizetti.

bio_en:
Emmanuel Pahud is a flutist born in Geneva, Switzerland, in 1970.

Pahud won the Geneva International Music Competition in 1992, and gained worldwide fame when appointed principal flutist of the Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra at the age of 22. Pahud is also active as a soloist.
style_en: A clear, elegant tone and perfect technique realize the delicacy and brilliance of the flute at once.

bio_en:
Sharon Bezaly is a flutist born in Tel Aviv, Israel, in 1972.

Bezaly has released numerous recordings on the BIS label and has contributed greatly to contemporary music, notably by commissioning and premiering works by contemporary composers.
style_en: Intense expressiveness and a warm tone underlie delicate interpretations of a wide repertoire from the classical to the contemporary.

bio_en:
Albrecht Mayer is an oboist born in Erlangen, Germany, in 1965.

Mayer gained worldwide fame as principal oboist of the Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra and has helped popularize the oboe as a solo instrument.
style_en: Playing that maximizes the warm, sweet tone of the oboe, marked by deep lyricism and fluent expressiveness.

bio_en:
Martin Fröst is a clarinetist born in Sweden in 1970.

Active as a world-class soloist, Fröst is said to have broadened the horizons of the clarinet solo repertoire, and is also famous for innovative performances that combine staging with performance.
style_en: Astonishing technique and varied tone color, combined with theatrical elements, show new possibilities for clarinet playing.

bio_en:
Sabine Meyer is a clarinetist born in Germany in 1959.

Meyer won worldwide fame as a woman wind player by serving as principal clarinetist of the Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra, and is also active as a soloist, contributing to the expansion of the clarinet repertoire.
style_en: A clear, clean tone and perfect technique; an orthodox player who shows deep insight in Classical repertoire.

bio_en:
Vadym Kholodenko is a pianist born in Ukraine in 1986.

Kholodenko won the Van Cliburn International Piano Competition in 2013 and gained international fame. His playing is regarded as combining outstanding technique with deep musicianship.
style_en: Dynamic playing with a strong attack and explosive energy, carrying the fiery emotion typical of the Russian school.

bio_en:
Beatrice Rana is a pianist born in Italy in 1993.

Rana drew attention by winning the Montreal International Competition in 2011 and the silver medal at the Van Cliburn International Piano Competition in 2013. Rana is counted one of Italy's leading young masters.
style_en: Outstanding technique and delicate sensibility underlie intellectual yet passionate interpretations of Classical and Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
Haochen Zhang is a pianist born in Shanghai, China, in 1990.

Zhang gained international fame by sharing first prize at the 2009 Van Cliburn International Piano Competition. His playing combines deep insight with astonishing technique.
style_en: An accurate, clear touch together with deep lyricism, and balanced playing achieved through a scholarly approach to the work.

bio_en:
Dmitri Masleev is a pianist born in Ulan-Ude, Russia, in 1987.

Masleev won the Tchaikovsky International Competition in 2015 and gained international fame. His playing is regarded as having outstanding technique and rich musicality, carrying on the tradition of Russian pianism.
style_en: Dazzling, overwhelming technique, explosive energy and the fiery emotion typical of the Russian school are combined in the playing.

bio_en:
George Li is a pianist born in Boston, USA, in 1995.

Li drew attention by winning the silver medal at the Tchaikovsky International Competition in 2015. A young master, Li combines lucid, clean interpretation with outstanding technique.
style_en: Accurate, intellectual interpretation and a bright, clean tone, with strengths in Classical and Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
Lukáš Vondráček is a pianist born in the Czech Republic in 1986.

Vondráček won the Queen Elisabeth Competition in 2016 and established an international reputation. Called a prodigy early on, Vondráček combines intense energy with deep musicianship.
style_en: Powerful, unrestrained attack together with deep lyricism, handling a broad repertoire freely.

bio_en:
Eric Lu is a pianist born in the United States in 1997.

Lu won the Leeds International Piano Competition in 2018 and drew worldwide attention. Lu is well received for restrained emotion and deep interpretation.
style_en: A lucid, deep touch and classical restraint reveal the structure and insight of a work.

bio_en:
Tianwa Yang is a violinist born in Beijing, China, in 1987.

At 13, Yang entered the Central Conservatory of Music in China as its youngest student, and drew attention for handling difficult repertoire flawlessly, such as a recording of Paganini's complete Caprices.
style_en: Accurate, brilliant technique, with outstanding ability particularly in works that demand a high level of virtuosity.

bio_en:
The Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra (BPO) is one of the world's finest orchestras, founded in Berlin, Germany, in 1882.

It has produced world-renowned masters as principal conductors, including Herbert von Karajan, Claudio Abbado and Simon Rattle. It is unrivaled in the interpretation of German Classical and Romantic repertoire.
style_en: The brass section is especially well developed, and the orchestra is known for the grand, rich “Berlin Philharmonic sound,” boasting intense expressiveness and a flexible ensemble.

bio_en:
The Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra (VPO) is one of the world's finest orchestras, founded in Vienna, Austria, in 1842.

It maintains a unique system in which the orchestra's members are drawn only from the Vienna State Opera. It is famous for its delicate, elegant Viennese sound, and is especially strong in Austro-German repertoire such as Mozart, Beethoven and Brahms.
style_en: The delicate, fluent tone of the strings stands out, and elegant, natural phrasing realizes the Romantic sound of the Viennese tradition.

bio_en:
The London Symphony Orchestra (LSO) is a world-class orchestra founded in London, England, in 1904.

One of Britain's leading symphony orchestras, it is well known to the general public through diverse activities such as film music recording. It is famous for innovative programs and flexible playing.
style_en: A flexible, versatile playing style, showing outstanding ability particularly in modern and contemporary music since the 20th century and in film music.

bio_en:
The Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra (RCO) is one of the world's finest orchestras, founded in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, in 1888.

Combined with the excellent acoustics of the Concertgebouw hall, it boasts a rich, organic sound. It is especially one of the leading orchestras in Mahler interpretation.
style_en: A warm, soft string ensemble and deep sound are its hallmarks, and it plays with an emphasis on fluent, organic flow.

bio_en:
The New York Philharmonic is the oldest orchestra in the United States, founded in New York in 1842.

Masters such as Gustav Mahler and Leonard Bernstein served as its principal conductors. Characterized by an intense, dynamic sound, it is one of America's “Big Five” orchestras.
style_en: A dynamic, brilliant and aggressive sound is its hallmark, with strengths especially in late Romantic and 20th-century repertoire.

bio_en:
The Chicago Symphony Orchestra (CSO) is a world-class orchestra founded in Chicago, USA, in 1891.

It was led by master conductors such as Georg Solti and Daniel Barenboim. Famous for the powerful sound of its brass section, it is one of America's “Big Five” orchestras.
style_en: The powerful, overwhelming sound of brass and percussion is its hallmark, and it boasts playing that combines precision with tremendous power.

bio_en:
The Boston Symphony Orchestra (BSO) is one of America's “Big Five” orchestras, founded in Boston, USA, in 1881.

Led by conductors of the French school such as Serge Koussevitzky and Charles Munch, it acquired French elegance and a refined tone.
style_en: French elegance and a fluent string sound are its hallmarks, with strengths especially in the interpretation of Impressionist music and 20th-century repertoire.

bio_en:
The Bavarian Radio Symphony Orchestra (BRSO) is a world-class orchestra founded in Munich, Germany, in 1949.

One of the major German orchestras, it was led by renowned conductors such as Rafael Kubelík and Mariss Jansons. It is well established in the interpretation of German Romantic repertoire.
style_en: It combines the deep, rich sound of the orthodox German school with a flexible, delicate ensemble, and is strong especially in late Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
The Dresden Staatskapelle is one of the oldest orchestras in the world, founded in Dresden, Germany, in 1548.

It was led by historic masters such as Richard Strauss and Karl Böhm. It has a unique tradition in German Romanticism, especially in the interpretation of Richard Strauss and Wagner.
style_en: It boasts a deep, dark, organic sound and traditional interpretation rooted in its long history, and is especially strong in Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
The Leipzig Gewandhaus Orchestra (GHO) is a venerable orchestra founded in Leipzig, Germany, in 1743.

It was led by masters such as Felix Mendelssohn and Arthur Nikisch. It maintains the authenticity of the German Classical-Romantic repertoire of Bach, Beethoven, Brahms and others.
style_en: A clear, transparent, balanced sound is its hallmark, and it shows deep interpretation in Classical and early Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
The Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra (SPO) is a top-level orchestra in Korea, founded in Seoul, South Korea, in 1948.

Welcoming world-class conductors such as Myung-Whun Chung as music director, it has grown into one of Asia's top orchestras. It plays a central role in Korea's classical music world.
style_en: It has a refined ensemble and the ability to handle a wide repertoire, and pursues a sound that is dynamic yet polished.

bio_en:
The KBS Symphony Orchestra (KBS SO) is a leading Korean orchestra founded in Seoul, South Korea, in 1956.

As part of KBS, it brings classical music to the public through public broadcasting. It boasts reliable playing and a wide range of activities.
style_en: It pursues a traditional, balanced sound and shows solid playing especially in German Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
The Korean Symphony Orchestra (KSO) is an orchestra founded in Seoul, South Korea, in 1985.

Together with the Korea National Opera, the Korea National Ballet and others, it contributes to the performing arts as a resident orchestra of the Seoul Arts Center. It handles a broad repertoire.
style_en: It is strong in opera and ballet accompaniment, and plays with an emphasis on dramatic expression and a flexible ensemble.

bio_en:
The Bucheon Philharmonic Orchestra is a municipal orchestra of South Korea, founded in Bucheon, Gyeonggi Province, in 1988.

With challenging projects such as conductor Hun-Joung Lim's performances of all the Mahler symphonies, it has built a distinctive domain in Korea's classical scene.
style_en: Based on serious, deep interpretation, it shows strong concentration and energy especially in large-scale late Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
The Daejeon Philharmonic Orchestra is a municipal orchestra founded in Daejeon, South Korea, in 1984.

It contributes to the development of local culture and the arts and builds its capabilities through performances in Korea and abroad.
style_en: It pursues solid, stable playing rather than showiness, and handles popular repertoire broadly.

bio_en:
The Busan Philharmonic Orchestra is a municipal orchestra founded in Busan, South Korea, in 1962.

As Busan's representative symphony orchestra, it is raising its international profile through overseas tours in Asia, Europe and elsewhere.
style_en: With lively, dynamic playing, it handles works from a wide range of periods and plays a central role in the local music scene.

bio_en:
The Incheon Philharmonic Orchestra is a municipal orchestra founded in Incheon, South Korea, in 1966.
