One of the municipal orchestras with a long history, it contributes to the cultural development of the Incheon area through a variety of special concerts and educational programs.
style_en: Based on a balanced ensemble and reliable playing, it presents a wide range from popular repertoire to large-scale works.

bio_en:
The Gwangju Symphony Orchestra is a municipal orchestra founded in Gwangju, South Korea, in 1976.

It represents classical music in the Gwangju area and also presents special performances tied to local history, such as a concert commemorating the May 18 Democratization Movement.
style_en: It is characterized by a powerful, serious sound, and is active especially in Korean new music and contemporary music from abroad.

bio_en:
The Suwon Philharmonic Orchestra is a municipal orchestra founded in Suwon, Gyeonggi Province, in 1982.

Centered on young, capable conductors, it is active and building recognition in Korea and abroad.
style_en: It pursues a flexible, refined ensemble and plays in a way that expresses well the varied colors of the Romantic era.

bio_en:
The Royal Philharmonic Orchestra (RPO) was founded in London, England, in 1946 by Sir Thomas Beecham.

One of London's four major orchestras, it has active recording activity and wide public recognition.
style_en: A brilliant, warm sound is its hallmark, and it boasts versatile playing that handles a broad repertoire.

bio_en:
The Philharmonia Orchestra was founded in London, England, in 1945 by Walter Legge.

From its early days it built its reputation by working with world-class conductors such as Karajan and Klemperer. It is one of London's leading orchestras.
style_en: It pursues precise, intellectual interpretation and a modern sound, and is especially strong in 20th-century repertoire.

bio_en:
The BBC Symphony Orchestra (BBC SO) was founded in London, England, in 1930 by the BBC.

A core orchestra of the BBC Proms, it plays an important role in a broad repertoire, especially in premieres of contemporary music.
style_en: It has a flexible, experimental playing style and an outstanding ability to realize contemporary music clearly and accurately.

bio_en:
The Munich Philharmonic is an orchestra founded in Munich, Germany, in 1893.

It played an historically important role, including premieres of Mahler's symphonies conducted by the composer. It has a deep tradition in the interpretation of German Romantic repertoire.
style_en: A deep, grand, warm sound is its hallmark, and it is strong especially in large-scale German Romantic works such as Bruckner and Mahler.

bio_en:
The WDR Symphony Orchestra was founded in Cologne, Germany, in 1947 as part of West German Broadcasting (WDR).

It is active in the 20th-century and contemporary repertoire and continues steady activity as a broadcast orchestra.
style_en: Based on a clean, clear ensemble, it shows the ability to take on contemporary music and unfamiliar repertoire boldly.

bio_en:
The NDR Elbphilharmonie Orchestra is an orchestra of North German Broadcasting (NDR), founded in Hamburg, Germany, in 1945.

Based at the Elbphilharmonie concert hall in Hamburg, it is drawing attention for vigorous, refined playing.
style_en: It pursues a dynamic, refined sound and a flexible ensemble, with strengths in 20th-century and contemporary repertoire.

bio_en:
The Orchestre de Paris was founded in Paris, France, in 1967 by Charles Munch.

It carries on the tradition of French music and holds an important position in the interpretation of 20th-century French repertoire.
style_en: It plays with an emphasis on brilliant, varied tone color and the delicate, refined phrasing typical of France.

bio_en:
The Orchestre National de France is an orchestra of French national radio, founded in France in 1934.

It has a deep tradition in the interpretation of French music, especially Impressionist works such as Debussy and Ravel.
style_en: A clear, transparent sound with rich color is its hallmark, and it shows the elegance and sensuous expression typical of French music.

bio_en:
The St. Petersburg Philharmonic is a leading Russian orchestra, founded in St. Petersburg, Russia, in 1882.

It was led by legendary conductors such as Yevgeny Mravinsky and has a unique tradition in the interpretation of Russian repertoire such as Tchaikovsky and Shostakovich.
style_en: Powerful, dark and intense expressiveness is its hallmark, and it delivers outstanding absorption in Russian Romantic and 20th-century large-scale works.

bio_en:
The Mariinsky Theatre Orchestra is Russia's finest opera and ballet theatre orchestra, founded in St. Petersburg, Russia, in 1783.

It gained worldwide fame under the baton of Valery Gergiev and holds the highest authority in the interpretation of Russian opera and ballet music.
style_en: Rich in dramatic and emotional expression, it boasts a flexible, brilliant sound optimized for opera and ballet music.

bio_en:
The Orchestra of the Accademia Nazionale di Santa Cecilia was founded in Rome, Italy, in 1908.

A leading Italian symphony orchestra, it has a deep tradition in Italian opera, such as Verdi and Puccini, and in symphonic repertoire.
style_en: Based on a rich, warm tone and a flexible ensemble, it emphasizes the melodic beauty and dramatic elements typical of Italian music.

bio_en:
The Czech Philharmonic is the Czech Republic's leading orchestra, founded in Prague, Czech Republic, in 1896.

It holds a unique position in the interpretation of works by Czech composers such as Dvořák and Janáček, and has Slavic lyricism.
style_en: A warm, human string sound and rich lyricism are its hallmarks, and it is strong especially in Czech and Slavic nationalist repertoire.

bio_en:
The Oslo Philharmonic is Norway's leading orchestra, founded in Oslo, Norway, in 1919.

Having produced world-class conductors such as Mariss Jansons, it built an international reputation beyond Northern Europe. It is strong in Nordic repertoire such as Sibelius and Grieg.
style_en: With a clear, clean tone and dynamic energy, it expresses the lyricism and vast scale typical of Northern Europe.

bio_en:
The NHK Symphony Orchestra (NHK SO) is a leading Japanese orchestra founded in Tokyo, Japan, in 1926.

As part of the Japanese broadcaster NHK, it plays a central role in Japan's classical music world and boasts a level of playing among the top in Asia.
style_en: Based on a precise, delicate ensemble and reliable playing, it mainly plays German and Russian Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
The Tokyo Metropolitan Symphony Orchestra (TMSO) is an orchestra founded in 1965 and belonging to the Tokyo Metropolis, Japan.

It contributes to the development of Tokyo's arts and culture and plays an active role especially in premieres of works by contemporary Japanese composers.
style_en: It pursues a modern yet balanced sound and has dynamic playing ability and the ability to handle a broad repertoire.

bio_en:
The Yomiuri Nippon Symphony Orchestra (YNSO) is an orchestra founded in 1962 under the Japanese newspaper company Yomiuri Shimbun.

One of Japan's major private symphony orchestras, it is active through regular concerts and overseas tours.
style_en: Based on a brilliant, fluent sound, it is strong especially in Russian Romantic and French repertoire.

bio_en:
The Singapore Symphony Orchestra (SSO) is an orchestra founded in Singapore in 1979.

One of Asia's leading orchestras, it plays repertoire spanning Eastern and Western musical traditions.
style_en: Based on a clean, precise ensemble, it plays in a way that harmonizes Eastern lyricism with Western grandeur.

bio_en:
The Hong Kong Philharmonic Orchestra (HK Phil) is an orchestra founded in Hong Kong in 1947.

One of Asia's most dynamic orchestras, it boasts programs spanning Eastern and Western music and outstanding playing.
style_en: Based on flexible, versatile playing, it excels at handling music from a variety of periods and genres.

bio_en:
The China Philharmonic Orchestra (CPO) is China's leading orchestra, founded in Beijing, China, in 2000.

It plays both Chinese music and major Western classical works and is quickly building an international reputation.
style_en: A powerful, grand sound combined with a melodic sensibility typical of China, and it is strong in Romantic repertoire.

bio_en:
The Shanghai Symphony Orchestra (SSO) is the oldest orchestra in Asia, founded in Shanghai, China, in 1879.

It has played an important role in the development of classical music in China and is currently recognized as one of Asia's major orchestras.
style_en: Based on a dynamic, refined sound, it balances traditional Western classical music and contemporary Chinese music.

bio_en:
The Philadelphia Orchestra is one of America's “Big Five” orchestras, founded in Philadelphia, USA, in 1900.

Under Leopold Stokowski it built a unique string sound known as the “Philadelphia Sound.”
style_en: A warm, rich, velvety string sound is its hallmark, and it has a unique tradition in the interpretation of Romantic-era repertoire.

bio_en:
The Cleveland Orchestra is one of America's “Big Five” orchestras, founded in Cleveland, USA, in 1918.

Under George Szell it gained worldwide fame for its precise, clear ensemble. It is especially strong in Classical and 20th-century repertoire.
style_en: A precise, clear and intellectual sound is its hallmark, and it boasts playing with a clean ensemble and perfect balance.

bio_en:
The San Francisco Symphony (SFS) is one of America's major orchestras, founded in San Francisco, USA, in 1911.

Under conductors such as Michael Tilson Thomas it drew attention for innovative programs and modern playing.
style_en: It has a vigorous, flexible playing style and shows outstanding adaptability especially in 20th-century and contemporary repertoire.

bio_en:
The Los Angeles Philharmonic (LA Phil) is an orchestra founded in Los Angeles, USA, in 1919.

Working with innovative conductors such as Gustavo Dudamel, it is active in contemporary music and new programs. It is one of America's major orchestras.
style_en: A bright, brilliant and dynamic sound is its hallmark, and it shows interpretation with a modern sensibility and a broad experimental spirit.

bio_en:
The Metropolitan Opera Orchestra is one of the world's finest opera orchestras, founded in 1883 as part of the Metropolitan Opera House in New York, USA.

Besides opera, it regularly plays symphonic concerts. It has unrivaled ability in opera accompaniment.
style_en: Based on a dramatic, flexible ensemble, it plays with a delicate yet powerful style optimized for singing and stage production.

bio_en:
The Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra (PSO) is an orchestra founded in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA, in 1895.

Under renowned conductors such as Fritz Reiner it acquired solid playing ability, and it is one of America's major orchestras.
style_en: Based on a balanced sound and precise ensemble, it handles a variety of repertoire from the classical to the Romantic.

bio_en:
The Toronto Symphony Orchestra (TSO) is Canada's leading orchestra, founded in Toronto, Canada, in 1922.

Active in Canada and abroad, it is recognized as one of North America's major orchestras.
style_en: It has a lively, dynamic playing style and handles a wide repertoire from the classics to contemporary Canadian works.

bio_en:
The Montreal Symphony Orchestra (OSM) was founded in Montreal, Canada, in 1935.

Under Charles Dutoit it gained worldwide fame for its interpretation of French repertoire. It is a major Canadian orchestra.
style_en: A clear, delicate and refined sound is its hallmark, and it beautifully expresses the varied colors typical of French music.

bio_en:
Sergei Tarasov is a world-class virtuoso pianist from the Tchaikovsky Moscow State Conservatory in Moscow, Russia. Having studied with the distinguished piano pedagogue Lev Naumov, Tarasov carries on the lineage of authentic Russian pianism. Tarasov has swept the world's most prestigious international competitions in succession and is nicknamed the “King of Competitions” and the “Grand Slammer.”

Currently a professor at Keimyung University in Daegu, South Korea, Tarasov combines teaching with performing, and is a pianist very familiar to Korean classical music fans.
style_en: A steel-like touch and a grand sound mark the playing. The power and technique typical of Russian pianists are in perfect harmony.

bio_en:
Krystian Zimerman is a Polish concert pianist and conductor, known as one of the finest pianists of his time. In 1975 he won the 9th International Chopin Piano Competition.

Zimerman was born in Zabrze, Poland, and studied in Katowice. His international career began with his victory at the Chopin Piano Competition in Warsaw in 1975. In 1976 he played with the Berlin Philharmonic conducted by Blomstedt. In 1979 he made his American debut with the New York Philharmonic. He has traveled extensively and made many recordings. From 1996 he taught piano at the music academy in Basel, Switzerland. In 1999, to commemorate the 150th anniversary of Chopin's death, he founded the Polish Festival Orchestra.

Zimerman now has a lifelong exclusive contract with Deutsche Grammophon (DG) and has released numerous acclaimed albums, including works by Beethoven, Brahms, Chopin, Debussy and Rachmaninoff. In particular, he made historic performances with legendary conductors such as Leonard Bernstein and Herbert von Karajan, and gave the premiere of Lutosławski's Piano Concerto, which was dedicated to him.
He performs as a soloist with the world's finest orchestras, including the Berlin Philharmonic and the Vienna Philharmonic, but strictly limits the number of performances each year in order to maintain perfect quality. He is famous for an obsession with sound and a strong perfectionism, to the extent of carrying around and assembling his own piano action himself to obtain the best sound.
style_en: A perfect structural beauty, rigorously calculated, and a crystal-clear, lucid touch, together with perfect control of explosive energy and delicate nuance, show an intellectual, analytical style of playing.

bio_en:
Born in Kyiv, Horowitz studied with Felix Blumenfeld at the Kyiv Conservatory and showed extraordinary genius from boyhood.

Escaping his homeland in the turmoil that followed World War I and the Russian Revolution, he made his debut as a pianist in Munich, Bavaria, in the German Empire in 1923, and the following year, 1924, made his formal debut in Berlin, in the German Empire; he then received overwhelming acclaim in London, England, and Paris, France. In 1928 he went to the United States and made a successful debut there, soon received wholehearted support from the famous conductor Toscanini, and eventually married Toscanini's daughter Wanda.

He was active in Europe and America afterward, but his health declined, and in 1953 he withdrew from the stage completely. In May 1965, however, he gave a “comeback” recital at Carnegie Hall and returned to the stage. Though somewhat frail in body, he had sharp fingertips and was said to excel at clear touch and to be dynamic. He also showed outstanding talent in producing refined yet forceful musical effects, such as in successions of octaves. However, it was always pointed out as his weakness that he did not devote himself to the works of a single composer. His tempo and rhythm were meticulous and exact, but in his later years, because of his health, a strongly subjective, romantic mood increasingly appeared in his music, and the tendency to treat his former firm tempo and rhythm freely grew more and more pronounced.

His acclaimed performances include Chopin's Scherzo No. 1, Barcarolle, Sonata No. 2 and Mazurkas; Liszt's Piano Sonata in B minor and “Vallée d'Obermann”; Schumann's Kinderszenen (Scenes from Childhood); Rachmaninoff's Piano Concerto No. 3 and Piano Sonata No. 2; Scriabin's Études, Preludes and Poèmes, and Sonata No. 9; and Scarlatti's sonatas.
style_en: A charismatic style that overwhelms audiences with the dynamics and diabolical virtuosity that come from a distinctive technique of playing with extended fingers, and with dreamlike, varied tone color.

bio_en:
Artur Rubinstein was a pianist from Łódź, Poland, born in 1887. Until the death in 1982, Rubinstein was loved as the most authoritative interpreter of Chopin and a symbol of the “happy pianist.”

Under the patronage of Joseph Joachim, Rubinstein studied in Berlin and made an early debut as a prodigy. In youth Rubinstein relied on genius and lived a dissipated life, and was criticized for lacking technical polish, but in middle age after marriage, after fierce practice, was reborn as a perfect master. This is regarded as a rare case in music history of a late-blooming genius.

As the flagship artist of the RCA Red Seal label, Rubinstein left the largest body of recordings in history. Having recorded almost all of Chopin's piano works, Rubinstein set the standard for modern Chopin interpretation, and was a true “man of iron” who traveled the world until nearly the age of 90 and performed on stage until eyesight almost failed, as well as a lover of drink, a gourmet, and an artist who loved life.

Rubinstein reflected on life and music in the following words:

“Music is simply my life. I live it, breathe it, talk it. I feel music almost unconsciously. No, I do not mean that I take it for granted. One must not take any gift of God for granted. But music is a part of me, like my arms and legs. Books, paintings, languages and people, on the other hand, are my passions, always to be cultivated. The same goes for travel. I am lucky to have a profession in which I can spend a lot of time on the road. On trains and planes I have time to read. So I am lucky to have become a pianist. The piano is a wonderful instrument. It is just the right size, so you cannot carry it around anywhere. So I can read instead of practicing. Am I not truly a lucky man?”
style_en: Phrasing as natural as flowing water and a warm, glossy tone known as the “golden tone” underlie a noble, masculine and lively style of playing that excludes excessive sentimentality.

bio_en:
Anna Borysivna Fedorova is a concert pianist from Ukraine. Fedorova performs as a soloist, a chamber musician and with symphony orchestras in major concert halls in many countries, including the Netherlands, Germany, France, Italy and the United Kingdom. Fedorova is a winner of the David Young Piano Prize and receives support from the Soirée d'Or Prize and the Keyboard Trust.

Fedorova was born in Ukraine and has wanted to be a pianist since the age of two. Fedorova began playing at five, gave a first public recital at six, and made a national debut at the National Philharmonic Society of Ukraine at seven.
Looking back on childhood, Fedorova said that there was always “the sound of the piano in the house,” because both parents were professional pianists. The parents gave Fedorova lessons, and Fedorova says that the parents played a decisive role in Fedorova's musical growth.

Fedorova has appeared at numerous international music festivals and has won top prizes in Italy, Greece, Germany, Slovakia, Estonia and the Czech Republic.
style_en: Always delicate, poetic and refined playing.
